annotation.speech2: The x y plane with a green circle of radius 2 centered at the origin, the constraint, and three circles centered at the point 1 comma negative 1, which are level curves of f. A small red circle, f equals 9 minus 4 root 2, is tangent to the constraint circle from inside at the point root 2 comma negative root 2. A large red circle, f equals 9 plus 4 root 2, is tangent to the constraint circle from outside at the point negative root 2 comma root 2. A dashed gray circle, f equals 7, crosses the constraint circle at two points. At each tangency point, red and green arrows show the gradients of f and g pointing in the same direction.
The constraint circle, x squared plus y squared equals 4, drawn in green, centered at the origin with radius 2.

The level curve f equals 9 plus 4 root 2, drawn in red: the largest circle centered at 1 comma negative 1 that still meets the constraint circle. It is tangent to it at negative root 2 comma root 2, where the absolute maximum is attained.

The level curve f equals 9 minus 4 root 2, drawn in red: the smallest circle centered at 1 comma negative 1 that meets the constraint circle. It is tangent to it at root 2 comma negative root 2, where the absolute minimum is attained.
The intermediate level curve f equals 7, drawn dashed in gray. It crosses the constraint circle at two points instead of being tangent, so the value 7 is attained but is not an extreme value.
The point 1 comma negative 1, the common center of the level curves of f and the location of the minimum of the unconstrained paraboloid.
The point negative root 2 comma root 2, where f attains its absolute maximum 9 plus 4 root 2 on the circle.
The point root 2 comma negative root 2, where f attains its absolute minimum 9 minus 4 root 2 on the circle.
The gradient of f at the maximum point, drawn in red, pointing away from the constraint circle in the same direction as the gradient of g. Here lambda equals 1 plus 1 over root 2.
The gradient of g at the maximum point, drawn in green, drawn slightly apart from the gradient of f so both are visible.
The gradient of f at the minimum point, drawn in red. It is shorter than the gradient of g, since lambda equals 1 minus 1 over root 2 is less than 1.
The gradient of g at the minimum point, drawn in green, collinear with the gradient of f.
